How's it hanging? That's a question that many people ask. And while the meaning of the phrase has changed over time, it always has to do with your mood. Let's see how it came to mean what it does today.
The first thing to understand is that the phrase had a completely different meaning a long time ago. Back then, if you were having difficulty hanging onto something, you were having difficulty hanging onto someone. The thing you were hanging onto was a cord, rope, or chain. The person you were hanging onto was your friend or your lover. So if you were having trouble holding on, it meant you were having trouble holding on to your friend or your lover.
In the 1800s, if you were in trouble, you could ask someone for help. If they were willing to help you, they would pull you out of the water with a rope. That's when the phrase "hang on to your life" came into use. It's still used today to mean the same thing. We just use it in a different way.
In the 1900s, people started using the phrase "hang on" to mean "hang on to it." That is, if someone was running away from you, he would shout, "hang on," to the person who was chasing him. And if someone was having trouble holding on to something, he would say, "hang on to your life."
The phrase "hang on to your life" was also used to mean "hang on to your money." In the 1930s, a movie about the Great Depression was made.
